findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on any I/O failure (missing file, permissions, etc.)
findings.failure_mode: untrusted or missing file path aborts the entire program instead of returning a typed I/O or parse error
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, _> and use .map_err(|e| MyError::Io(e)) or an equivalent typed error; never call unwrap on fallible I/O

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on any non-numeric payload or out-of-range value
findings.failure_mode: malformed CSV row aborts the program instead of returning a typed Invalid/Parse error for the offending record
findings.fix: use .parse::<u32>().map_err(|_| MyError::Invalid) and propagate through a Result return type; remove unwrap

findings.problem: as u16 is a lossy cast: any u32 value > 65535 silently truncates
findings.failure_mode: out-of-range value silently wraps to an incorrect u16, producing a corrupted Record with no error signal
findings.fix: use u16::try_from(value).map_err(|_| MyError::Invalid) or check range explicitly before constructing Record

findings.problem: parts[0] is unchecked indexing into a Vec produced by split(',').map().collect()
findings.failure_mode: empty line or line with no comma produces Vec with length < 2, panicking on index access instead of returning a typed error
findings.fix: use split_once(',') and .ok_or(MyError::Invalid) or iterator-based access with .nth(0)/.nth(1) plus checked indexing

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) is a side effect inside the mapping closure of a data-parsing function
findings.failure_mode: pure-looking function has observable I/O side effects, breaking determinism, testability, and the functional-core imperative-shell boundary
findings.fix: move all I/O (println, file reads, network calls) into a separate shell layer; the parsing core should be a pure function returning a Result or Option

findings.problem: load_frames combines file I/O (fs::read_to_string) with data parsing and domain construction in a single function
findings.failure_mode: cannot unit-test parsing logic in isolation; any test must touch the filesystem; violations of the pure-core / imperative-shell boundary
findings.fix: split into (a) a pure parse_line(line: &str) -> Result<Record, _> function and (b) a shell function load_frames(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, _> that reads the file, delegates to parse_line, and handles I/O errors

findings.problem: No try_reserve on the output Vec; every intermediate line also allocates a Vec<String> via collect()
findings.failure_mode: large input files can OOM; intermediate per-line Vec allocations are unnecessary overhead
findings.fix: compute capacity from line count or known max; call values.try_reserve(max).map_err(|_| MyError::Allocation)?; replace per-line Vec<String> collect with split_once + &str slicing

findings.problem: load_frames returns Vec<Record> with no error type; all failure modes (I/O, parse, out-of-range, indexing) are hidden behind panic
findings.failure_mode: caller has no way to distinguish or handle specific failure modes; the domain has no error taxonomy
findings.fix: define a typed error enum (e.g. enum FrameError { Io(std::io::Error), Invalid, TooMany, Overflow, Allocation }) and change the return type to Result<Vec<Record>, FrameError>

findings.problem: value is a raw u16 with no domain constraint enforcement at the type level
findings.failure_mode: any code path can construct a Record with an invalid value; the type system cannot enforce domain invariants
findings.fix: use a newtype like pub struct RecordValue(u16) with a fallible constructor that validates domain constraints, making illegal states unrepresentable

findings.failure_mode: cannot verify performance claims or allocation behavior; intermediate Vec allocations and string clones may be costly at scale
findings.fix: add a micro-benchmark with workload characterization, baseline measurement, and allocation tracking (e.g. criterion or similar)
